newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares reverse course, end down on FII sales.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares reverse course, end down on FII sales.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed sharply lower as heavy selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) wiped out modest midsession gains, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index ended down 9.35 points at 639.64.
"The bearish phase gathered momentum as purchases by domestic financial institutions failed to arrest the declining trends," said Sumit Gandhi of brokers Rare Financial Services.
Traders said lower prices on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) also affected sentiment. The BSE's main index closed 38.65 points lower at 2,851.85.
ACC lost 34 rupees to close at 973.0 on heavy speculative selling, brokers said.
TELCO plunged 23.70 rupees, or 7.45 percent, to 294.30 on heavy selling by FIIs coupled with profit-taking by speculators, they said.
Reliance Industries closed 0.25 rupee lower at 181.25.
Larsen and Toubro lost 2.70 rupees to 211.50.
ITC bucked the trend and rose 1.40 rupees to 275.15 on selective foreign buying, brokers said.
